english: Let $S$ be the set of all complex numbers $z$ satisfying $\arg\left(\dfrac{z-1}{z+1}\right)=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$, where $\arg$ denotes the principal argument. Then the set of all values of $|z-3+2i|$ for $z\in S$ is
hindi: माना कि $S$ उन सभी सम्मिश्र संख्याओं $z$ का समुच्चय है जो $\arg\left(\dfrac{z-1}{z+1}\right)=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ को संतुष्ट करती हैं, जहाँ $\arg$ मुख्य कोणांक (principal argument) को दर्शाता है। तब $z\in S$ के लिए $|z-3+2i|$ के सभी मानों का समुच्चय है
solution: $S$ is the arc from which the chord joining $-1$ and $1$ subtends $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$; for $z=iy$ the argument is $\pi-2\tan^{-1}y$, so the arc is above the real axis
Central angle $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$: radius $\dfrac{2}{2\sin(\pi/4)}=\sqrt{2}$, centre $c=i$; $S$ is the part of $|z-i|=\sqrt{2}$ with $\mathrm{Im}\,z>0$ (end points $\pm1$ excluded)
$p=3-2i$: $|p-c|=|3-3i|=3\sqrt{2}$, so on the full circle $|z-p|$ runs from $3\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{2}=2\sqrt{2}$ to $3\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{2}=4\sqrt{2}$
Farthest point $c+\sqrt{2}\cdot\dfrac{c-p}{|c-p|}=i+(-1+i)=-1+2i$ lies on the arc, so $4\sqrt{2}$ is attained
Nearest point $c+\sqrt{2}\cdot\dfrac{p-c}{|p-c|}=i+(1-i)=1$ is an excluded end point, so $2\sqrt{2}$ is not attained; near $z=1$ the values come arbitrarily close to it
The arc is connected, so all values in between occur: the set is $(2\sqrt{2},4\sqrt{2}]$
solution_full: For $z\neq\pm1$, $\arg\left(\dfrac{z-1}{z+1}\right)$ is the angle through which the vector from $-1$ to $z$ must turn to reach the vector from $1$ to $z$, that is, the angle subtended at $z$ by the segment from $-1$ to $1$, taken with sign.
For $z=iy$, $y>0$: $\arg(iy-1)-\arg(iy+1)=(\pi-\tan^{-1}y)-\tan^{-1}y=\pi-2\tan^{-1}y\in(0,\pi)$. So the argument is positive above the real axis, and the locus is an arc in the upper half-plane.

An arc on which a chord of length $2$ subtends $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ belongs to a circle in which the chord subtends $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ at the centre. So $2=2r\sin\dfrac{\pi}{4}$, $r=\sqrt{2}$, and the centre is at distance $\sqrt{r^{2}-1}=1$ from the chord.

Since the inscribed angle $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ is acute, the arc is the major arc and the centre is on the same side as the arc: $c=i$. Check: $z=i(1+\sqrt{2})$ gives $\pi-2\tan^{-1}(1+\sqrt{2})=\pi-\dfrac{3\pi}{4}=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$.
Hence $S=\{z:|z-i|=\sqrt{2},\ \mathrm{Im}\,z>0\}$; the points $\pm1$ are not in $S$ because the quotient is undefined at $-1$ and is $0$ at $1$.

Let $p=3-2i$. Then $|p-c|=|3-3i|=3\sqrt{2}>\sqrt{2}$, so $p$ is outside the circle. By the triangle inequality, for every $z$ on the circle, $3\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{2}\leq|z-p|\leq3\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{2}$, with equality at the two ends of the diameter through $p$.
The far end is $c+\sqrt{2}\cdot\dfrac{c-p}{|c-p|}=i+\sqrt{2}\cdot\dfrac{-3+3i}{3\sqrt{2}}=-1+2i$, which has $\mathrm{Im}=2>0$, so it lies on the arc and $|z-p|=4\sqrt{2}$ is attained.
The near end is $c+\sqrt{2}\cdot\dfrac{p-c}{|p-c|}=i+(1-i)=1$, which is excluded. So $2\sqrt{2}$ is not attained, but points of the arc close to $1$ give values as close to $2\sqrt{2}$ as we like.
At the other end point $-1$ (also excluded) the value would be $|-4+2i|=2\sqrt{5}<4\sqrt{2}$, which does not affect the range.
The arc is connected and $|z-p|$ is continuous, so every value between the infimum and the maximum occurs. The set of values is $(2\sqrt{2},4\sqrt{2}]$.
originality_note: New: an argument-locus arc whose nearest point to the given point is an excluded end point, so the triangle-inequality minimum is an infimum and the range is half-open (way 5, the link between the arc's end points and the extremum is the discovery). Closest known: maximum and minimum of |z - p| on a circle. Different because: the student must decide which arc, check that the far extremum lies on it and that the near one is an excluded end point.
